opportunities.description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Location: Austin, Texas, US

Available Term: Winter (January - April 2027)

About the Role

The team is building AI agents for the People team that can reason, act, and coordinate without constant human input. You will contribute to this foundation and gain firsthand experience. We value fundamentals, curiosity, and fast learning. Join the People Innovation Lab to rapidly build and deploy internal enterprise applications and tooling for the Cloudflare People & Places organization, focused on making work smarter.

What We Provide

• Opportunity to solve real problems with AI and code.

• Mentorship, dedicated manager, regular 1:1s, and structured support.

• Real sprint work with production deliverables.

• Access to Cloudflare's full intern cohort (community, events, network).

• A portfolio artifact: production-deployed code and a shipped product demo.

What You'll Build & Do

• You will build production features in a sprint-based team.

• Work is guided by the IT Customer Zero team and deployed on Cloudflare infrastructure.

• Strong fundamentals and fast ramp-up ability are essential.

• Build and ship full-stack features, clean production code, and integrations for internal tools.

• Write and review code, work in sprints (managing tickets/blockers), and coordinate with the other intern.

• Effectively use AI-assisted coding tools.

• Demo working products to leadership.

Requirements & Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

• Pursuing CS, Software Engineering, or related degree (or equivalent experience).

• Ability to build and demonstrate a working web application.

• Proficient in JavaScript/TypeScript and comfortable with one back-end language/framework.

• Solid understanding of end-to-end web app functionality (HTTP, APIs, data persistence, deployment).

• Experience with shared codebases such as Git and meaningful commits.

• Ability to commit to a full-time (40 hours/week Monday - Friday) for a minimum 12 week internship.

• In office 3-5 days a week.

Preferred Qualifications

• Familiarity with serverless/edge computing.

• Experience with a modern front-end framework (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.) and/or MCPs/APIs, data modeling, or systems design (for back-end seat).

• Experience using AI-assisted development tools (Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode).

• Prior sprint-based team experience.

• For UI seat: Experience with design systems, Figma, or strong interaction design sense.

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

Figma employees are among the most AI-active in the industry, and our Internal AI team, part of FTS (our Business Technology org), helps turn that energy into meaningful impact by making it easier for every Figmate, from Sales and Support to Finance, People, and Legal, to safely adopt AI and use it to improve how they work.

We’re a small, high-leverage team organized around three pillars: Platform & Tooling, Infrastructure & Hosting, and Applied AI Builds, and this role is a key member of the Applied AI Builds pillar.

As an AI Engineer, Internal Tools, you’ll work directly with teams across Figma to identify high-value AI opportunities and take them to production, moving from understanding a business workflow, to rapidly prototyping an approach, to evaluating it and integrating it with the systems and data needed to make it useful in the real world.

This isn’t a role focused only on building AI demos: you’ll own solutions through production, help determine where AI adds value and where traditional rules-based software is the right choice, and shape how agents can safely take actions across enterprise systems. As common patterns emerge, you’ll partner with our Platform & Tooling and Infrastructure teams to build reusable capabilities that make future AI builds faster and safer.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

• Partner directly with teams across GTM, Finance, People, Legal, Support, and other business functions to understand workflows and identify high-value opportunities for AI

• Design, build, and productionize AI agents, assistants, and workflow automations that solve real business problems using LLMs, tool calling, RAG, structured outputs, agent frameworks, MCP, APIs, and enterprise data

• Integrate AI applications with enterprise systems and data sources across GTM, Finance, People, Support, and internal APIs

• Build evaluations and feedback loops to measure accuracy, reliability, and business impact before and after AI solutions reach production

• Design deterministic guardrails, human-in-the-loop controls, and approval patterns for workflows where AI systems take business-critical actions

• Build production-ready systems with strong observability, failure handling, security, authentication, authorization, and auditability

• Identify reusable patterns across individual AI projects and build them out as shared components and capabilities in partnership with our Internal AI platform teams

• Help define how Figma approaches Applied AI engineering and scales AI adoption across the company

We’d love to hear from you if you have:

• 5+ years of software engineering experience building production applications, integrations, backend systems, or AI-powered products

• Hands-on experience building applications with LLMs, agents, retrieval-augmented generation, function calling, schema-constrained outputs, or evaluation frameworks

• Experience taking an AI application or workflow beyond a prototype and operating it in a production environment

• Strong API, integration, and system design fundamentals, with experience connecting applications across multiple systems and data sources and strong engineering judgment about when to apply AI and when a rules-based approach is the right choice, and experience designing reliable production systems with appropriate observability, failure handling, authentication, authorization, and security controls

• Experience working directly with non-engineering stakeholders to understand ambiguous business problems and translate them into technical solutions and ability to move quickly from discovery to prototype while understanding what is required to safely and reliably productionize a solution

While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

• A background building internal AI applications or working in an Applied AI, Forward Deployed Engineering, or AI Solutions Engineering role

• Experience with MCP, agent orchestration frameworks, and enterprise tool-calling patterns

• Knowledge of AWS Bedrock, AgentCore, OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar AI platforms

• Experience integrating enterprise systems such as Salesforce, Zendesk, Workday, NetSuite, Greenhouse, or Slack

• Knowledge of with AI evaluations, observability, prompt/version management, and human-in-the-loop systems

• Experience implementing enterprise identity and access patterns such as Okta, SSO, OAuth, and secure service-to-service authentication, within Security, Privacy, SOX/ITGC, or other enterprise governance requirements

questions.explanation: The native structuredClone() API performs a structured clone algorithm supporting Dates, Sets, Maps, and cyclical references, unlike JSON serialization.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Promise.all and Promise.allSettled?
options: Promise.all runs sequentially, whereas Promise.allSettled runs in parallel
Promise.all rejects immediately upon the first rejection, whereas Promise.allSettled waits for all promises to resolve or reject
Promise.all returns an array of status objects, whereas Promise.allSettled returns only raw values
Promise.allSettled is deprecated in modern Node.js runtimes
questions.explanation: Promise.all fast-fails when any promise rejects. Promise.allSettled waits for every promise to settle and provides an array describing the outcome of each.

questions.question: In TypeScript, what is the key benefit of using 'unknown' over 'any'?
options: 'unknown' disables all type checking just like 'any'
'unknown' requires type narrowing or type assertion before operations can be safely performed on the value
'unknown' can only represent primitive types
'unknown' is only valid in server-side Next.js code
questions.explanation: 'unknown' is the type-safe counterpart of 'any'. You cannot access arbitrary properties or invoke methods on an 'unknown' value without narrowing its type first.

quizzes.title: Relational Database Design & Indexing
quizzes.description: Tests knowledge of B-Tree indexing rules, ACID isolation, foreign key constraints, and query plan performance.

questions.question: Given a composite B-Tree index on (department_id, graduation_year, cgpa), which query will NOT be able to utilize this index efficiently?
options: WHERE department_id = 'CSE' AND graduation_year = 2026
WHERE department_id = 'CSE'
WHERE graduation_year = 2026 AND cgpa > 8.0
WHERE department_id = 'CSE' AND graduation_year = 2026 AND cgpa > 8.0
questions.explanation: B-Tree composite indexes require queries to filter on the leading columns (leftmost prefix). A query filtering only on 'graduation_year' skips 'department_id' and cannot use the index tree traversal efficiently.

questions.question: In ACID transaction guarantees, which isolation level prevents Dirty Reads and Non-Repeatable Reads, but allows Phantom Reads in standard ANSI SQL?
options: Read Uncommitted
Read Committed
Repeatable Read
Serializable
questions.explanation: Repeatable Read ensures that any row read during a transaction cannot be modified by another transaction. In traditional ANSI SQL, new rows matching a range query (phantom reads) could still appear unless Serializable is used.

questions.question: Why should you avoid placing an index on a low-cardinality boolean column like 'is_active' in a 1,000,000-row table?
options: Boolean indexes are not supported in modern relational databases
The query optimizer will usually favor a sequential scan because half the rows match anyway
Boolean indexes corrupt database transaction logs
Boolean values cannot be balanced in a B-Tree node
questions.explanation: When a column has low selectivity (cardinality), the query planner calculates that traversing index pages plus random heap lookups is slower than a sequential block scan.

questions.question: What is the key criterion for a database table to satisfy Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)?
options: It must contain no composite primary keys
For every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey
It must store all array relationships in JSONB columns
It must have exactly one foreign key per table
questions.explanation: BCNF is a stricter version of 3NF where every determinant (left side of any non-trivial functional dependency) must be a superkey of the relation.

questions.question: What is connection pool starvation in database systems?
options: When memory on the database server runs out due to large temp tables
When all available pool connections are held by active or slow queries, causing new requests to queue or timeout
When the database drops network connections after idle timeout
When replication lag prevents secondary replicas from accepting read queries
questions.explanation: Connection starvation happens when web workers acquire database connections and hold them during slow external API calls or unindexed queries, blocking other HTTP requests from obtaining a connection.

quizzes.title: Modern React & Frontend Architecture
quizzes.description: Evaluates React 19 / Next.js App Router patterns, hooks lifecycle, reconciliation, and Core Web Vitals.

questions.question: Why is using array index as a 'key' prop considered an anti-pattern when rendering dynamic lists in React?
options: It causes compile errors in React 19
Reordering or deleting items causes React to misidentify component identities, leading to incorrect state retention and DOM churn
Array indices cannot be cast to strings in JSX
It disables React concurrent memoization completely
questions.explanation: Keys tell React which item is which across renders. When using indices, deleting or reordering shifts index positions, causing React to associate old component instance states with new data items.

questions.question: In Next.js App Router, which file convention defines a fallback UI rendered automatically via React Suspense while route segments load?
options: error.tsx
loading.tsx
skeleton.tsx
page.loading.tsx
questions.explanation: Next.js automatically wraps page components in a React <Suspense fallback={<Loading />}> boundary when a loading.tsx file exists in the route segment folder.

questions.question: How do you avoid race conditions when fetching data inside a client component useEffect hook without an external library?
options: Set the dependency array to [Date.now()]
Use a boolean 'ignore' / 'cancelled' flag in the effect cleanup function to disregard out-of-order resolved promises
Wrap the fetch call in a synchronous while-loop
Declare the effect callback as 'async () => {}'
questions.explanation: By setting `let cancelled = false; return () => { cancelled = true; }`, if inputs change before the previous network call finishes, the previous promise result is discarded safely.

questions.question: In modern CSS Flexbox, why might text truncation ('truncate' / 'text-overflow: ellipsis') fail inside a flex child?
options: Flex children default to 'min-width: auto', which prevents shrinking below content size unless 'min-width: 0' is applied
Ellipsis is only supported in grid layouts
Flex containers cannot have text nodes
The browser requires 'display: inline-flex' for truncation
questions.explanation: By default, flex children have `min-width: auto`, which forbids the child from shrinking smaller than its intrinsic content width. Setting `min-width: 0` allows flex items to shrink and trigger text truncation.

questions.question: Which Core Web Vital measures the time from when the user initiates navigation to when the largest image or text block within the viewport is rendered?
options: Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
Time to First Byte (TTFB)
questions.explanation: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures perceived loading speed and marks the point in the page load timeline when the primary content has likely loaded.

quizzes.title: Python, Pandas & Machine Learning Foundations
quizzes.description: Tests vectorization, EDA, model evaluation metrics, and general machine learning engineering practices.

questions.question: Why is vectorized computation in NumPy and Pandas significantly faster than native Python for-loops over arrays?
options: Vectorized functions execute compiled C/Fortran code in contiguous memory blocks with SIMD hardware instructions and avoid Python GIL overhead per element
NumPy automatically uploads data to an external cloud cluster
Python for-loops convert every number to a string internally
Vectorized code runs exclusively on GPUs
questions.explanation: NumPy arrays are stored in contiguous C memory buffers and vectorized operations execute compiled machine code using CPU SIMD instructions, avoiding dynamic Python type-checking and interpreter overhead on each iteration.

questions.question: In an imbalanced binary fraud detection problem where positive fraud cases are only 0.2% of the dataset, why is standard Accuracy a deceptive metric?
options: Accuracy cannot be calculated on float values
A naive dummy classifier predicting 'Not Fraud' 100% of the time achieves 99.8% accuracy while failing to detect a single fraudulent case
Accuracy requires equal numbers of features and rows
Scikit-learn disallows accuracy on binary targets
questions.explanation: With extreme class imbalance, a model that classifies everything as the majority class has high accuracy but zero recall. Precision-Recall AUC or F1-Score are far more informative.

questions.question: What does it indicate if the training loss continues to decrease steadily while validation loss starts increasing after epoch 12?
options: The model is underfitting the training distribution
The model is overfitting to noise in the training set and losing generalization power
The learning rate is too low
The dataset has zero bias
questions.explanation: Divergence between decreasing training loss and increasing validation loss is the canonical signature of overfitting. Early stopping should halt training at this inflection point.

questions.question: Why should feature scaling parameters (e.g. mean and standard deviation in StandardScaler) be fit ONLY on the training split, and not on the entire dataset?
options: To avoid data leakage from the test set into the model training pipeline
Because test sets cannot contain negative values
Because StandardScaler only accepts 100 rows at a time
To allow the test set to normalize itself independently
questions.explanation: Fitting scalers or imputers on the full dataset leaks test set statistics into the training phase, giving an unrealistically optimistic estimate of true out-of-sample performance.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between standard K-Fold and Stratified K-Fold cross-validation?
options: Stratified K-Fold ensures each fold maintains the same percentage of target class labels as the complete dataset
Stratified K-Fold works only on continuous regression targets
Standard K-Fold is deterministic, while Stratified is random
Stratified K-Fold trains on all folds at the same time
questions.explanation: Stratification preserves class proportions across all cross-validation folds, which is vital for preventing folds with missing or skewed representation of minority classes.
